chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭāhirī, who said:

Al-Mutawakkil became ill from an abscess that appeared on him, and because of it he came near to destruction. No one dared to touch him with iron. So his mother vowed that if he were cured, she would carry to Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام a great amount from her wealth. Al-Fatḥ ibn Khāqān said to him, “If only you would send to this man and ask him, for it may well be that he has a description of a remedy by which relief may come to you.”

So he sent to him عليه السلام and described his illness to him. The messenger returned to him with the instruction that the pressed residue of sheep fat should be taken, mixed with rosewater, and applied to it. When the messenger returned and informed them, they began mocking his statement. Al-Fatḥ said to him, “By Allah, he is more knowledgeable concerning what he said.” So the residue was brought, and it was prepared as he had said and applied to it. Sleep overcame him and he became calm. Then it opened and what had been inside it came out, and his mother was given glad tidings of his recovery.

So she carried to him عليه السلام ten thousand dinars under her seal. Then he recovered from his illness, and al-Baṭḥāʾī al-ʿAlawī informed against him that wealth and weapons were being carried to him عليه السلام. So he said to Saʿīd the chamberlain, “Attack him at night, take whatever wealth and weapons you find with him, and bring it to me.”

Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad said: Saʿīd the chamberlain said to me, “I went to his house at night, and I had with me a ladder. I climbed to the roof, and when I descended partway down the steps in the darkness, I did not know how to reach the house. Then he called to me, ‘O Saʿīd, stay where you are until they bring you a candle.’ It was not long before they brought me a candle. So I descended and found that he was wearing a woolen cloak and a woolen cap, and there was a sajjādah upon a mat before him. I had no doubt that he was performing salat (prayer).”

He said to me, ‘The rooms are before you.’ So I entered them and searched them, but I found nothing in them. I found the purse in his house sealed with the seal of the mother of al-Mutawakkil, and another sealed bag. He said to me, ‘The place of salat (prayer) is before you.’ So I lifted it and found a sword in an unsheathed cover. I took that and went to him. When he looked at his mother’s seal on the purse, he sent for her and she came out to him.

Some of the special servants informed me that she said to him, ‘I had made a vow during your illness, when I had despaired for you, that if you recovered I would carry to him ten thousand dinars from my wealth. So I carried it to him, and this is my seal on the bag.’ He opened the other bag and there were four hundred dinars in it. So he added to the purse another purse and ordered me to carry that to him عليه السلام. So I carried it, and I returned the sword and the two bags, and I said to him, ‘O my master, this weighed heavily upon me.’
So he said to me: “And those who have done ظلم will come to know to what overturning they shall be overturned.”

key_terms.الْبَدْرَةَ: a purse or bag of money
key_terms.الْمُصَلَّى: the place of salat (prayer) or prayer rug
key_terms.خَاتَمِهَا: her seal or signet used to mark the bag
key_terms.خُرَاجٍ: an abscess or boil causing severe illness
key_terms.ظَلَمُوا: they acted unjustly or committed oppression
key_terms.كُسْبُ الشَّاةِ: the pressed residue or extract from sheep fat used as a remedy
key_terms.نَذَرَتْ: she made a vow contingent upon recovery

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith about al-Mutawakkil’s illness show the knowledge and dignity of Imam ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report narrates the illness of al-Mutawakkil, his cure through the instruction of Imam ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, and the later attempt to seize wealth and weapons from the Imam’s residence. It highlights the Imam’s knowledge, composure, and spiritual station, while ending with a Qur'anic warning concerning the fate of the oppressors.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Tahiry who said,

‘Al-Mutawakkil (the Caliph) fell sick from an abscess than came out with him, and faced the death due to it. No one had the boldness that he touches him with an iron (to perform surgery). So his mother vowed if he is cured, she would carry over to Abu Al-Hassan Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, a stately portion from her wealth, and Al-Fat’h Bin Khaqan said to him, ‘If only you would send to this man (10<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) and ask him<sup>asws</sup>, for he<sup>asws</sup> would not be devoid that there would happen to be in his<sup>asws</sup> possession a remedy for you to be relieved by it’.

Therefore, he sent a message to him<sup>asws</sup> and described his illness to him<sup>asws</sup>. A messenger returned to him with: ‘Take an oil extracted from a sheep’s fat mixed with rose extracts and warm it with water and place it upon it (the boil)’. So when the messenger returned and informed them, they turned around mocking at his<sup>asws</sup> words. So Al-Fat’h said to him (Al-Mutawakkil), ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He<sup>asws</sup> is more knowing with what he<sup>asws</sup> said’, and he brought the oil extracts and prepared it just as he<sup>asws</sup> has said, and placed upon it. So the sleep overcame him and he settled. Then it (the boil) split, and whatever was in it came out, and his mother was given the glad tidings of his recovery.

So she carried over ten thousand Dinars to him<sup>asws</sup> sealed with her insignia. Then he fully recovered from his illness, so Al-Bat’hai Al-Alawy informed him that (large amounts of) wealth is being carried over to him along with weapons. So he said to Saeed the guard, ‘Raid upon him<sup>asws</sup> at night and seize whatever you find with him<sup>asws</sup> from the wealth and the weapons, and carry it over to me’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Ibrahim Bin Muhammad said, ‘So Saeed the guard said to me, ‘I went to hisasws house at night and with me was a ladder. So I ascended to the rood. So when I descended upon one of the level in the darkness, I did not know how I could arrive to the house. So heasws called out to me: ‘O Saeed! (Stay) in your place until they bring you the candle’. So it was not long before I was given a candle. So I descended and I found himasws to have a woollen coat upon himasws, and a woollen cap of it, and there was a prayer mat upon a carpet in front of himasws. So I did not doubt that heasws was Praying Salat.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Besides you there are rooms’. So I entered these and investigated them but I could not find anything therein, and I found the bag in his<sup>asws</sup> house sealed by a seal of the mother of Al-Mutawakkil, and a (another) sealed bag. And he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Beside you is the prayer mat. So I raised it and I found a sheathed sword without a covering. So I seized that and went over to him (Al-Mutawakkil). So when he looked at the seal of his mother upon the bag, he sent a message to her. So she came out to him.

So, one of the specials servants informed me that she said to him, ‘It was so that I had vowed regarding your illness due to what you lived from it, and if you recover, I would carry over to him from my own wealth, ten thousand Dinars. So I carried it over to him, and this is my seal upon the bag’. And he opened the other bag, and there were four hundred Dinars. So he merged these with the bag, another bag, and instructed me to carry that over to him<sup>asws</sup>. So I carried it and returned the sword and the two bags, and I said to him, ‘O my Master<sup>asws</sup>! (This is) hurtful upon me’.
So heasws said to me: [26:227] and they who act unjustly shall come to know the turning they shall be Overturned with’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah from Ali ibn Muhammad from Ishaq al-Jallab who has said the following.

“Once I bought a large number of sheeps for abu al-Hassan (a.s.). He called and admitted me into the barn area of his house into a vast location that I could not recognize. He ordered me to distribute the sheep among certain people and of such people were abu Ja‘far and his mother and others.

Thereafter I requested permission to leave for Baghdad to see my father. It was the day of Tarwiya (eighth of the month of Dhi al-Hajj). He wrote to me, “Stay with us tomorrow thereafter leave.” I stayed that day and then it was the day of ‘Arafa (ninth of Dhi al-Hajj but I stayed with them that day as well as the tenth night in the balcony of his house. At dawn he came to me and said, “O Ishaq, wake up.” I then got up.”
The narrator has said that I then opened my eyes and found myself at my own door in Baghdad.

I went inside and met my father and I was among my people and I told them I spent the day of ‘Arafa (ninth of Dhi al-Hajj) in the army camp (Samarra) and for ‘Id (tenth of Dhi al-Hajj) I am in Baghdad.”
